diagram_math_checks.details: Under the unchanged equivalent conditions N is normal in G, G=NH, N∩H={1}. Put E=N⋊αH. Diagram arrows are i:N→E, i(n)=(n,1); ι:N→G, ι(n)=n; π:E→H, π(n,h)=h; q:G→H, q(nh)=h; Φ:E→G, Φ(n,h)=nh; outer vertical arrows are identity maps. Existence and uniqueness of nh follow from proof steps 1.2 and 2.1, so q is well-defined.

The external law in def-external-semidirect-product and thm-external-semidirect-product-is-a-group is (n,h)(n′,h′)=(n α_h(n′),hh′). Here α_h(n′)=hn′h^{-1}, exactly as Statement and step 1.2. Normality ensures α_h:N→N is an automorphism (L2); α_h α_k=α_hk by conjugation composition, so this is a left action. Then (nh)(n′h′)=n(hn′h^{-1})hh′, with no reversal of h,h′.

Left square: Φ∘i(n)=Φ(n,1)=n=ι(n). Right square: q∘Φ(n,h)=q(nh)=h=π(n,h). Both comparisons use identity outer arrows. The central isomorphism mark is justified by proof steps 1.2 and 2.1, which prove Φ a bijective homomorphism.

The product law gives π((n,h)(n′,h′))=hh′ and q((nh)(n′h′))=hh′. Hence π,q are homomorphisms; ker π=i(N) and ker q=N since h=1 characterizes their kernels. i and ι are injective homomorphisms. The sections j:H→E, j(h)=(1,h), and s:H→G, s(h)=h, are homomorphisms by the canonical-factor supplier and subgroup inclusion. π∘j=q∘s=id_H and Φ∘j=s hold pointwise. These explain split rows; no N-directed retraction or commuting-factor claim is made.

The original rigorous numbered proof remains identical except two blank-line removals in step 1.2. Neither proof nor Statement invokes the new figure. All new relations follow directly from the existing formulas and unique decomposition.
